chapter_title: Chương 83: 0083【Nguyên Bồi lớp là cái quái gì?】

segments.title: Chương 83: 0083【Nguyên Bồi lớp là cái quái gì?】
segments.content:
Back in the countryside, I lay around for a day, not wanting to do anything.

The next day, early in the morning.

My cousin, Chen Guirong, came to the door with some Termitomyces mushrooms. "My mom picked these chicken mushrooms, brought some over for you."

"Thanks," Chen Guiliang said casually, "how are your preparations for the high school entrance exam going?"

Chen Guirong replied stiffly, "They're okay."

After some thought, his cousin added, "Bro, why don't you try to persuade my parents? I'm just not cut out for studying. I want to go to a vocational school to learn a skill and start working to earn money sooner. They insist I go to high school, but I just can't focus on my studies!"

Chen Guiliang had no desire to get involved. "You can try high school first. If it really doesn't work out, you can drop out after a year and transfer to a vocational school."

Chen Guirong thought for a moment. "That's not a bad idea."

The kid was about to take his exams, yet he was in a completely relaxed state. He cheerfully went home and brought back two lift nets.

These lift nets were very small, made from old mosquito nets, and could only be used to catch small fish and shrimp.

A childish whim suddenly struck Chen Guiliang. He made bait from rapeseed meal, cornmeal, and wheat flour, and went with his cousin to the riverside to catch river shrimp for fun.

It was thanks to more than half the city's factories closing down. If it were a few years ago, this little river would have been a stinking sewer.

Of course, severe pollution had its "benefits."

Especially in summer, when factories would collectively discharge waste during heavy rainstorms. The sewage would come and stun the fish. Farmers downstream would rejoice; even the elderly and children would bring out their hand nets to scoop up the half-dead fish to take home and eat.

Having grown up eating fish from polluted water, Chen Guiliang had long been tested by the periodic table, his body already forged to be immune to all poisons.

A Nokia ringtone sounded.

Chen Guiliang put down his hand net and pulled his phone from his pocket.

"Hello, this is Hu Weishi."

"Hi, Sister Weishi."

"How do you feel about the college entrance exam?"

"It was okay. I should be able to get over the Tier 1 university cutoff."

"Then I wish you a happy life at Peking University in advance. Do you have any plans to write a novel? Li Haiyang, who won the first prize with you, has already started writing one."

"I'll think about it."

"The sci-fi piece you wrote for the preliminary round could totally be expanded into a novel."

"What about a historical novel?"

"That could work too. Send me the first few chapters to take a look at."

"I'll prepare it then."

"..."

After hanging up, his cousin looked at him with envy.

Chen Guirong said, "Bro, you're so awesome. You have a cell phone even while you're still in school."

"I bought it with my own manuscript fees," Chen Guiliang said. "If you can get into a junior college, I'll give you a cell phone."

"Really?" Chen Guirong suddenly didn't want to go to vocational school anymore.

"Why would I lie to you?"

By mid-morning, the sun grew stronger, and the weather became hotter.

Chen Guiliang carried home two or three catties of river shrimp.

"Meow~~~"

Panda'er smelled the fishy scent from afar and dashed over, weaving around his legs.

Chen Guiliang grabbed a handful of river shrimp and casually tossed them on the ground. The little cat feasted with great relish.

In the afternoon, Chen Guiliang took a bus to the city and headed straight for the Xinhua Bookstore.

As expected, he only found a dusty set of the History of Ming in a forgotten corner.

As for things like the Veritable Records of the Ming Dynasty, they were impossible to buy and couldn't be found online either. Finding research materials in this era was a painful process.

What was Chen Guiliang planning to do?

*Those Things of the Ming Dynasty*, of course.

Chen Guiliang had only written up to the second chapter of that cyberpunk novel before putting it aside. First, it was difficult to write; second, it was destined to have few readers.

Because he wanted to stuff too much of his personal views into it!

*Those Things of the Ming Dynasty* had a good market. The content was simple enough; as long as you weren't illiterate, there was no reading barrier.

Of course, what Chen Guiliang wrote would certainly be different from the original author, Dangnian Mingyue.

He couldn't even remember the college entrance exam essay topic, let alone the details of *Those Things of the Ming Dynasty*. He had to go through the source materials himself and write it slowly, borrowing the original author's creative method—that is, writing a historical novel full of interesting tidbits.

Yes, *Those Things of the Ming Dynasty* is considered a novel.

Out of personal likes and dislikes, Teacher Dangnian Mingyue had added quite a bit of his own private interpretation into it.

Chen Guiliang wasn't very fond of some of that interpretation. For example, portraying the famous official Zhang Cong as something akin to a villain was really a bit outrageous.

But for a novel, it was completely understandable.

*Romance of the Three Kingdoms* blackened Zhou Yu's name to such an extent, and *Ming Dynasty in 1566* portrayed Zhao Zhenji as a non-stick pan. This didn't stop *Romance of the Three Kingdoms* and *Ming Dynasty* from being exceptionally brilliant.

Chen Guiliang chose to write *Those Things of the Ming Dynasty* not just to earn manuscript fees.

He wanted to pave the way for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*!

An RPG game like *The Legend of Mir* required too much startup capital, and the development cycle was also long.

*Legends of the Three Kingdoms* was different. It could be launched quickly with low costs.

Moreover, the game's lifespan was long enough.

Twenty years later, when you thought it was completely dead, it had actually transformed into a pay-to-win game, with monthly revenue maintaining around 300 million yuan.

Chen Guiliang could totally rely on *Those Things of the Ming Dynasty* to build up his fame and fanbase, then launch the *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* game and physical cards in due course.

Hmm, he could also use Peking University as a promotional platform for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*!

"Liangliang, still reading after the college entrance exam?" His mother, Yao Lan, walked over and asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Just some leisure reading to relax."

Yao Lan glanced at the *History of Ming*, a dense row of books. She didn't think this stuff could be relaxing.

But she was very happy that her son was always so self-motivated in his studies.

For the next twenty days or so, Chen Guiliang spent his days flipping through the *History of Ming*, copying down content he thought was useful.

He couldn't start writing immediately just yet. He was pondering where to get a copy of the *Veritable Records of the Ming Dynasty*.

It wasn't available on the market right now, but Peking University's library would definitely have it.

In the blink of an eye, it was June 27th.

Chen Guiliang took a rural bus, slowly making his way back to school to check his scores and fill out his university choices.

Seeing the familiar school gate again, Chen Guiliang was filled with emotion.

Peking University, Admissions Office.

A Director Zhu, who shouldn't have been here, was in the admissions office, calling the top scorers from each province one by one.

"Hello, is this student Yang XX? Congratulations on achieving the top score in science for the entire province. I'm from the Peking University Admissions Office. Oh, you want to apply to Tsinghua? Actually, you could also consider Peking University, especially Peking University's Yuanpei Program. Our teaching methods here are very special..."

"Hello, may I ask if this is XXX High School? I'm from the Peking University Admissions Office. Congratulations to your school's student for winning the provincial top score in liberal arts. Could you please have student Zhou XX come to the phone for a chat..."

Another Deputy Director Lu walked in. "How's it going?"

"Let's talk outside," said Director Zhu.

Director Lu asked, "How many top scorers are willing to come to the Yuanpei Program?"

Director Zhu said, "About twenty-something said they would consider it, but only two have committed."

"Expanding the Yuanpei Program to 160 students this year, I'm afraid we've taken too big a step," Director Lu sighed.

Director Zhu said, "I'll contact the top ten in liberal arts and sciences from each province one by one."

The first cohort of Peking University's Yuanpei Program recruited students after the school year had already begun. Students from any department could transfer in, as long as they passed the interview.

It was rather chaotic at the time, and the major departments had quite a few complaints—they were not happy about having their top students poached by the Yuanpei Program.

Starting from the second cohort, they were forced to switch to pre-enrollment recruitment.

For example, when Chen Guiliang filled out the application form for Peking University's independent recruitment, the first choice on the list of available programs was the Yuanpei Program.

But Chen Guiliang had filled in the Department of Philosophy.

Also, for national first-prize winners and international gold medalists in math, physics, and chemistry competitions, as long as they were guaranteed admission to Peking University, the Yuanpei Program would fight for them!

This year, the Yuanpei Program had already secured 20 students guaranteed admission for winning national first prizes in academic competitions, three of whom had also won gold medals in the International Chemistry Olympiad.

The Yuanpei Program also had to fight for the top scorers in liberal arts and sciences from each province, grabbing as many as they could.

Director Lu said, "We could also recruit Chen Guiliang."

"The one who caused a lot of controversy a while back?" Director Zhu asked.

Director Lu nodded. "We can't fill all the spots anyway, and he's very suitable for the Yuanpei Program."

Director Zhu smiled. "That's true. The Yuanpei Program is indeed lacking students like him. I'm very much looking forward to his performance after he enrolls."

"Minister Cheng's side..." Director Lu reminded him.

"I'll go ask for him," Director Zhu said.

Director Lu chuckled. "It's got nothing to do with me. I was just mentioning it offhand."

Director Zhu said, "You continue contacting the top ten from each province. I'll pay Minister Cheng a visit. Suddenly expanding to 160 spots was indeed a bit ill-considered. It'll be good if we can enroll 150 this year."

Minister Cheng was also busy at this time.

The moment he saw Director Zhu, he was instantly on alert. "Who are you trying to snatch this time?"

Director Zhu, all smiles, respectfully refilled Minister Cheng's teacup. "What do you mean 'snatch'? You make it sound like we're bandits."

"Cut the crap, just spit it out," Minister Cheng said, not giving him a pleasant look.

Director Zhu said, "I want to pick someone from the independent recruitment list."

Minister Cheng asked, "Which one?"

"Chen Guiliang," said Director Zhu.

Minister Cheng said, "He applied for the Department of Philosophy through independent recruitment."

Director Zhu said, "Since he likes philosophy, he can choose a philosophy specialization in his sophomore year. Won't he end up in your hands then, Minister Cheng?"

Minister Cheng said irritably, "Who the hell knows what you'll turn him into. He might just run off to pick physics, chemistry, or computer science in his sophomore year for all I know. There's been more than one or two cases like that. I had a perfectly good provincial top scorer in liberal arts, and last year you guys got him to major in materials science!"

"He chose it himself, we didn't force him," Director Zhu said with a grin. "Besides, didn't we also send you an international chemistry gold medalist guaranteed admission to major in history and philosophy?"

Hearing this, Minister Cheng's expression softened slightly.

Director Zhu continued, "If Minister Cheng is worried that Chen Guiliang might go astray, you can assign him a top philosophy professor as a part-time mentor. Professor Xu Lai would be very suitable."

Minister Cheng flew into a rage. "You're trying to snatch my professors now too?"

"A part-time mentor, it won't take up much time," Director Zhu said.

Director Zhu shamelessly pestered him for half the day, and Minister Cheng finally couldn't stand it anymore. "You call Chen Guiliang yourself and see what he wants."

"Haha, thank you, leader."

"Go, go, go, stop bothering me!"

(The mentors and students in the Yuanpei Program, some names are sensitive and can easily get censored. All names used in the book are fictional.)
